name: IT services and support
description: Managed IT for businesses: services, support packages, references and clients' questions, with facts about the area served, support hours, response times, the emergency line, remote support and the systems you look after.

questions.question: Where do you come on site – which towns or how far from your office?
questions.help: For example "Ostrava and up to 50 km; remote support anywhere".

questions.question: When is your support available?
questions.help: For example "Mon–Fri 8–18; outside these hours only on the Premium package".

questions.question: How quickly do you respond to a reported problem?
questions.help: Exactly as your contracts state it, e.g. "urgent: within 2 working hours, other: next working day". Never stronger than the contract.

questions.question: Which number should clients call when something critical breaks?
questions.help: Leave it empty if you have no emergency line.

questions.question: Where do clients download your remote support tool?
questions.help: The download address of the tool you use for remote sessions. Leave it empty if you do not use one.

questions.question: Which systems and platforms do you look after?
questions.help: For example "Windows, macOS, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Synology, networks and printers".

questions.question: Which vendor partnerships or technical certifications do you currently hold?
questions.help: Only partner levels and certifications you actually hold today. Leave it empty if there are none.

questions.question: Since which year have you been in business?

audit.message: State your response time – it is what businesses compare IT providers by.
Say where you come on site – clients outside your area should know before they ask.
Add your support packages with what each covers – a monthly price helps clients decide.
Add the services you offer, each with what it includes.
Fill in your phone number in Business details – when the IT stops, clients call.
Publish a privacy policy page – you work with your clients' systems and data; check what your law requires.

claude: Businesses choosing an IT provider want to know whether you look after systems like theirs, how fast you react, what it costs per month and whom to call when something breaks – so the support packages, response time, support hours and the emergency line belong near the top, kept as facts so they read the same as in the contracts. Support packages go in the plans collection with the same wording of what is covered across packages; "on request" when the price depends on the number of devices. Write calmly and concretely, without fear-based selling. Never invent response times, uptime, vendor partner levels, certifications, clients or references, and never promise "100 % secure" or "no data loss". When a client may have legal duties (data protection, cybersecurity rules), say they should be checked rather than stating what the law requires.
